build: build fcfac709, policyengine-uk 2.177.7, certified in policyengine 6.20.2

measures.name: Health element and PIP removal for young people, from April 2027 (combined)
measures.description: The health element removal for under-25s (all claimants) and the PIP removal for 18 to 24-year-olds simulated together, with their interactions.

measures.name: Health element removal with severe cases kept and PIP at half rate, from April 2027 (combined)
measures.description: The health element removal for under-25s with severe cases kept, and PIP at half rate for 18 to 24-year-olds in place of a new additional cost allowance, simulated together with their interactions.

measures.name: UC health element removed for under-25s
measures.description: From April 2027 Universal Credit awards no longer include the health (LCWRA) element where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 25, for existing and new claimants alike; an award keeps it where a joint claimant aged 25 or over has that capability. The assessment itself is unchanged, so the work allowance still applies, but an award without the element loses the benefit cap exception that rests on it.

measures.name: UC health element removed for under-25 new claims
measures.description: From April 2027 Universal Credit awards paid the health element at the new-claimant rate (claims from April 2026) no longer include it where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 25; protected claimants keep it. The data hold no claim dates: the model assigns the new-claimant rate by a random draw at the expected share of claims, regardless of age, so the figure rests on that assumption.

measures.name: PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds
measures.description: From April 2027 people aged 18 to 24 receive neither component of Personal Independence Payment; 16 and 17-year-olds keep it and Disability Living Allowance for children is unchanged. Entitlements that depend on receiving PIP go with it. Scottish recipients of Adult Disability Payment, which the data record as PIP, are included.

measures.name: Under-25 UC standard allowance at the 25-and-over rate
measures.description: From April 2027 single Universal Credit claimants under 25 receive the standard allowance for those aged 25 and over, and couples in which both are under 25 receive the couple rate for those aged 25 and over. The protected health element is held at its current-law amount, which the law otherwise links to the under-25 allowances. The report proposes a Youth Allowance at the under-25 rate, higher only for those living independently; this run shows the higher rate for every under-25.

measures.name: Employer NICs zero rate extended to under-25s
measures.description: From April 2027 employers pay no Class 1 National Insurance on earnings up to the upper secondary threshold (£50,270 a year) for employees under 25, extending the zero rate for under-21s. The model passes employers' National Insurance through to wages, so the saving shows as higher pay for these employees. The report considers this option and does not propose it (paragraph 268); it proposes a higher threshold for 21 to 24-year-olds in retail and hospitality instead.

measures.name: UC health element removed for under-22s
measures.description: From April 2027 Universal Credit awards no longer include the health (LCWRA) element where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 22, for existing and new claimants alike: the age limit proposed in the 2025 Pathways to Work green paper.

measures.name: UC health element removed for under-25s, severe cases kept
measures.description: As the removal for under-25s, except that a young claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity who scores 24 or more PIP daily living points (about a fifth of young PIP recipients) keeps the element. The points stand in for the report's Severe and Complex Needs Insurance, for which the report gives no eligibility test.

measures.name: PIP at half rate for 18 to 24-year-olds
measures.description: From April 2027 people aged 18 to 24 receive half their current Personal Independence Payment. This is an illustrative stand-in for the report's Additional Cost Allowance, for which the report gives no rates; Scottish Adult Disability Payment, recorded as PIP, is included. Half an award can fall below the amounts that qualify a carer for Carer's Allowance or a household for disability premia, so those can be lost too; a new allowance could carry its own qualifying rules.

measures.name: PIP removed for 16 to 24-year-olds
measures.description: As the PIP removal for 18 to 24-year-olds, but from age 16: 'under 25' read literally. Disability Living Allowance for children under 16 is unchanged.

measures.name: Health element and PIP removal from April 2027, phased as claimants are reassessed
measures.description: The health element and PIP removals for young people, reaching people who turned 18 since April 2026 at once, and existing claimants as they are reassessed, at an assumed 25% of those remaining each year. Who is reassessed is a random draw, as the data hold no reassessment dates.

measures.name: Health element and PIP removal from April 2027, with an illustrative move into work
measures.description: The full package, with a randomly chosen quarter of affected young people who do not work (aged 18 to 24, with PIP or limited capability for work and work-related activity) moving into 16 hours a week at their minimum wage. An illustrative scenario, not an estimate of how people would respond.

measures.name: Health element and PIP removal for young people, from April 2029 (combined)
measures.description: Two of the report's benefit changes, simulated together with their interactions and without its replacement payments: UC health element removed for under-25s; PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds. The report's other modelled measures, such as the higher Youth Allowance, are separate runs.

measures.name: UC health element removed for under-25s
measures.description: From April 2029 Universal Credit awards no longer include the health (LCWRA) element where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 25, for existing and new claimants alike; an award keeps it where a joint claimant aged 25 or over has that capability. The assessment itself is unchanged, so the work allowance still applies, but an award without the element loses the benefit cap exception that rests on it.

measures.name: PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds
measures.description: From April 2029 people aged 18 to 24 receive neither component of Personal Independence Payment; 16 and 17-year-olds keep it and Disability Living Allowance for children is unchanged. Entitlements that depend on receiving PIP go with it. Scottish recipients of Adult Disability Payment, which the data record as PIP, are included.

measures.name: Employer NI threshold of £10,000 for 21 to 24s in retail and hospitality
measures.description: The report's end state: employers pay Class 1 National Insurance on earnings above £10,000 a year, not £5,000, for employees aged 21 to 24 whose main job is in retail (SIC division 47) or hospitality (divisions 55 and 56). The 15% rate is unchanged, and under-21s and apprentices under 25 keep their zero rate. The report gives no start date or costing and proposes a five-year glide path; the end state is shown in every year. policyengine-uk holds each employer's total cost of employment fixed, so the saving passes to employees as higher pay; hiring does not respond.

measures.name: Higher Youth Allowance for under-25s living independently
measures.description: From April 2029 Universal Credit claims in which every adult is under 25 and that include a housing costs element are paid the standard allowance for those aged 25 and over, the review's own proxy for living independently (analytical annex, section 8). Other young claims keep the under-25 rate, which the report proposes as the Youth Allowance's base level. The report gives no amount for its work allowance, so none is modelled.

measures.name: Health element and PIP removal from April 2029, phased as claimants are reassessed
measures.description: The report's health element and PIP changes for young people, reaching people who turned 18 since April 2028 at once, and existing claimants as they are reassessed, at an assumed 45% of those remaining each year. Who is reassessed is a random draw, as the data hold no reassessment dates.

measures.name: Employer NI threshold for 21 to 24s in retail and hospitality, phased in
measures.description: The report's five-year glide path, in assumed equal steps from April 2027: the employer National Insurance threshold for employees aged 21 to 24 whose main job is in retail (SIC 47) or hospitality (SIC 55 and 56) is £6,000 in 2027-28, rising £1,000 a year to £10,000 in 2031-32. The report gives no start date or steps. The 15% rate is unchanged; the saving passes to pay.

measures.name: Child Disability Living Allowance extended to 18
measures.description: From April 2029, 16 and 17-year-olds stay on child Disability Living Allowance (DLA) instead of moving to Personal Independence Payment (PIP) at 16 (report para 760). Modelled as a swap at the equivalent award level: PIP daily living at the standard or enhanced rate becomes the DLA care component at the middle or highest rate, and PIP mobility at the standard or enhanced rate becomes DLA mobility at the lower or higher rate. Each pair has the same weekly amount, so awards do not change in the model. The data do not record who would keep, lose or change an award without the reassessment at 16, so that effect is not estimated. Scottish records are left as they are: Child Disability Payment is already paid to 18.

measures.name: Work allowance for under-25s in work (illustrative)
measures.description: From April 2029 every Universal Credit claim in which all claimants are under 25 has a work allowance: earnings below it do not reduce the award. The report proposes a work allowance for everyone on the Youth Allowance who is in employment (para 749) and gives no amount. The amount here is our assumption: the current Universal Credit work allowance, the lower rate for claims with a housing costs element and the higher rate for those without, uprated each year. Claims that already have a work allowance (with a child or limited capability for work) keep it, and the 55% taper and the standard allowance are unchanged.

measures.name: Child DLA extended to 18
measures.description: 16 and 17-year-olds stay on Disability Living Allowance instead of moving to PIP (report paragraph 760).
measures.reason: DLA and PIP pay the same amounts, so the switch changes no payment; its effect on reassessment is not in the data.

measures.name: Additional Cost Allowance
measures.description: A national, non-means-tested allowance for established, ongoing disability costs, replacing PIP for young people.
measures.reason: Its eligibility and rates are not in the model.

measures.name: Severe and Complex Needs Insurance
measures.description: A stable long-term income, above today's maximum benefit rates, where paid work is not realistic.
measures.reason: The data cannot identify who would qualify, and its rate is not in the model.

measures.name: Local Health and Disability Fund
measures.description: Local payments for one-off or changing disability costs, decided by the Youth Opportunity Service.
measures.reason: Awards are at local discretion, with no rule to apply to households.

measures.name: Duty to engage
measures.description: Persistent refusal to engage can end in loss of the Youth Allowance.
measures.reason: It works through behaviour, which a static model omits.

measures.name: Care Leaver Transition Allowance
measures.description: A six-month weekly allowance for care leavers who are NEET or at serious risk.
measures.reason: The model's data do not identify care leavers.

measures.name: Opportunity Guarantee
measures.description: A legal right to education, training or work, with a paid six-month job as backstop.
measures.reason: An entitlement to places, not a tax or benefit rule.

measures.name: Hiring payments to employers
measures.description: Payments to employers for hiring a young person who has been out of work and education for six months.
measures.reason: Its effect is on hiring, which a static model omits.

measures.name: Apprenticeship target
measures.description: More apprenticeship starts for under-25s a year by 2036, with pre-apprenticeship places.
measures.reason: A target for places, not a tax or benefit rule.

measures.name: Further education places
measures.description: More 18 to 24-year-olds in further education each year, over the decade.
measures.reason: A spending programme, not a tax or benefit rule.
